science.title: Why CoQ10 matters
science.text: Every cell has mitochondria — tiny engines that turn food into ATP, your body's energy currency. CoQ10 (coenzyme Q10) is essential to that process, and it doubles as a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress. Your natural levels fall with age and can be lowered by certain medications, so topping up with 200 mg of ubiquinone supports energy, heart health and everyday vitality.

items.a: Coenzyme Q10 is a compound your body makes and your mitochondria use to produce cellular energy (ATP). It's also an antioxidant. Levels naturally fall with age, which is why many people supplement it.
This is ubiquinone, the most-studied and most stable form of CoQ10. Your body converts it into ubiquinol as needed.
CoQ10 is fat-soluble, so taking it with a meal that has some fat significantly improves how much you absorb.
Yes — it's in a vegetable (hypromellose) capsule with no animal ingredients.
It's popular with older adults, people on statin medication (which can lower CoQ10), and anyone wanting to support energy and heart health — but check with your physician if you take medication.
